notes.summary: This chapter covers the determinant of square matrices up to order 3, minors and cofactors, the adjoint and inverse of a matrix, the area of a triangle using determinants, and solving systems of linear equations by the matrix method, including deciding whether a system is consistent. CBSE tests quick determinant and adjoint/inverse computations, results such as |kA| = kⁿ|A| and |adj A| = |A|ⁿ⁻¹, and the consistency of systems.
keyPoints: |[[a, b], [c, d]]| = ad − bc. For a 3 × 3 determinant, expand along any row or column using the sign pattern + − + / − + − / + − +; choose the row or column with the most zeros.
Minor Mᵢⱼ = determinant left after deleting row i and column j; cofactor Aᵢⱼ = (−1)ⁱ⁺ʲ Mᵢⱼ. E.g. in [[2, −3], [4, 5]], M₂₁ = −3 and A₂₁ = +3.
adj A = transpose of the cofactor matrix. For a 2 × 2 matrix, adj [[a, b], [c, d]] = [[d, −b], [−c, a]] (swap the diagonal entries, change the signs of the other two).
A(adj A) = (adj A)A = |A| I, and A⁻¹ = (1/|A|) adj A exists only if |A| ≠ 0 (non-singular matrix).
For an n × n matrix: |kA| = kⁿ|A|, |AB| = |A||B|, |A⁻¹| = 1/|A|, |adj A| = |A|ⁿ⁻¹. E.g. n = 3 and |A| = 2 give |3A| = 27 × 2 = 54.

Area of a triangle with vertices (x₁, y₁), (x₂, y₂), (x₃, y₃) = ½ |x₁(y₂ − y₃) + x₂(y₃ − y₁) + x₃(y₁ − y₂)|. Zero area means the points are collinear; when the area is given, use both the + and − values.

System AX = B: if |A| ≠ 0, there is a unique solution X = A⁻¹B. If |A| = 0 and (adj A)B ≠ O, the system is inconsistent (no solution). If |A| = 0 and (adj A)B = O, it may have infinitely many solutions or none.
A matrix identity such as A² − 4A + I = O gives A⁻¹ = 4I − A after multiplying both sides by A⁻¹ (valid when |A| ≠ 0).
traps: Forgetting the minus sign of the middle term while expanding a 3 × 3 determinant along a row.
Writing |kA| = k|A| instead of kⁿ|A| for an n × n matrix.
Forgetting to transpose the cofactor matrix while forming adj A.
Taking only the positive value when an area is given — |expression| = 8 gives two equations.
Concluding 'no solution' as soon as |A| = 0 without checking (adj A)B.
notes.examTip: For any inverse or system question, find |A| first: if it is 0, the inverse does not exist and there is no unique solution — this alone often eliminates two options.

questions.text: The value of the determinant |[[1, 2, 0], [0, 3, 1], [2, 0, 1]]| is:
questions.explanation:
Expand along the first row: 1 × (3·1 − 1·0) − 2 × (0·1 − 1·2) + 0 × (0·0 − 3·2).
= 1 × 3 − 2 × (−2) + 0.
= 3 + 4 = 7.
(Forgetting the minus sign of the middle term gives 3 − 4 = −1.)

questions.text: For the matrix [[2, −3], [4, 5]], the minor M₂₁ and the cofactor A₂₁ of the element a₂₁ = 4 are:
questions.explanation:
Deleting row 2 and column 1 leaves only the entry −3, so M₂₁ = −3.
A₂₁ = (−1)²⁺¹ × M₂₁ = (−1) × (−3) = 3.
So M₂₁ = −3 and A₂₁ = 3.

questions.text: If the area of the triangle with vertices (k, 0), (4, 0) and (0, 2) is 4 square units, then:
The system of linear equations x + 2y = 2 and 2x + 4y = 3 is:
questions.explanation:
Write the system as AX = B with A = [[1, 2], [2, 4]] and B = [[2], [3]].
|A| = 4 − 4 = 0, so there is no unique solution.
adj A = [[4, −2], [−2, 1]], and (adj A)B = [[8 − 6], [−4 + 3]] = [[2], [−1]] ≠ O.
Since |A| = 0 and (adj A)B ≠ O, the system is inconsistent.

questions.text: Using the matrix method, the solution of the system 2x + 5y = 1 and 3x + 2y = 7 is:

Assertion (A): If A is a 3 × 3 matrix with |A| = 2, then |3A| = 6.
Reason (R): For a square matrix A of order n and a scalar k, |kA| = kⁿ|A|.
Choose the correct option.
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false
Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true
questions.explanation:
R is a standard result: in kA every one of the n rows is multiplied by k, so |kA| = kⁿ|A|.
For n = 3: |3A| = 3³ × |A| = 27 × 2 = 54, not 6.
So A is false and R is true.

questions.text: If A = [[2, 3], [1, 2]] satisfies A² − 4A + I = O, then A⁻¹ equals:
questions.explanation:
|A| = 4 − 3 = 1 ≠ 0, so A⁻¹ exists.
Multiply A² − 4A + I = O by A⁻¹: A − 4I + A⁻¹ = O, so A⁻¹ = 4I − A.
4I − A = [[4 − 2, 0 − 3], [0 − 1, 4 − 2]] = [[2, −3], [−1, 2]].
The formula (1/|A|) adj A gives the same matrix.

questions.text: The values of x for which |[[x, 1, 1], [1, x, 1], [1, 1, x]]| = 0 are:
questions.explanation:
Expand along the first row: x(x·x − 1·1) − 1(1·x − 1·1) + 1(1·1 − x·1).
= x³ − x − x + 1 + 1 − x = x³ − 3x + 2.
x³ − 3x + 2 = (x − 1)²(x + 2).
So the determinant is 0 when x = 1 or x = −2.
